subject: classical-statistical-mechanics

external_suppliers.interface:
Fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$ and a finite nonempty alphabet $A$. A configuration is a function $\sigma:\mathbb Z^d\to A$. An interaction list consists of a finite index set $\mathcal R$ and, for each $r\in\mathcal R$, a finite nonempty shape $S_r\subset\mathbb Z^d$ containing $0$ and a function $\Phi_r:A^{S_r}\to\mathbb R$. The index $r$ is part of the data: two equal shapes with different indices represent two terms and are both counted. Every translate $x+S_r$ contributes once, with value $\Phi_r((\sigma_{x+y})_{y\in S_r})$.

The range is $R=\max_{r\in\mathcal R}\operatorname{diam}_\infty(S_r)$, with $R=0$ when $\mathcal R$ is empty. For finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$, define the free-volume energy and the energy conditioned on an exterior configuration $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$ by
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}_\Lambda(\sigma)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:x+S_r\subseteq\Lambda}\Phi_r(\sigma_{x+S_r}),\qquad E_\Lambda(\tau_\Lambda\mid\eta)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal R}\ \sum_{x:(x+S_r)\cap\Lambda\ne\varnothing}\Phi_r((\tau_\Lambda\eta)_{x+S_r}).$$
Here $\tau_\Lambda\in A^\Lambda$, and $\tau_\Lambda\eta\in A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ is the concatenated configuration equal to $\tau_\Lambda$ on $\Lambda$ and to $\eta$ on $\Lambda^c$.
These are finite sums: for each finite shape $S_r$, only finitely many anchors $x$ make $x+S_r$ meet $\Lambda$. Terms meeting $\Lambda$ but not contained in it appear in the conditional energy and not in the free-volume energy. The definitions are mathematical and assign no physical units; a physical model must state its units separately.

external_suppliers.interface:
Assume the Axiom of Choice [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. A **finite reversible stochastic rate model** consists of an integer $r\ge2$, the finite state set $E=\{1,\ldots,r\}$, real energy parameters $e_a\in\mathbb R$, an inverse-energy parameter $\beta>0$, and finite transition rates $w_{ab}\ge0$ for distinct $a,b\in E$. When physical units are assigned, $e_a$ is measured in joules, $\beta$ in joules$^{-1}$, and $w_{ab}$ in seconds$^{-1}$; this mathematical definition does not assert a physical realization. Define

$$Z:=\sum_{a\in E}e^{-\beta e_a},\qquad \pi_a:=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta e_a}.$$

Then $Z$ is finite and positive, and $\pi$ is a strictly positive probability vector. Require $w_{ab}>0$ exactly when $w_{ba}>0$, require the undirected graph with edge $\{a,b\}$ whenever $w_{ab}>0$ to be connected, and impose detailed balance $\pi_aw_{ab}=\pi_bw_{ba}$. Define the row generator $Q$ by $Q_{ab}=w_{ab}$ for $a\ne b$ and $Q_{aa}=-q_a$, where $q_a:=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}$. Since $r\ge2$ and the graph is connected, every $q_a>0$. Thus $(Qf)_a=\sum_{b\ne a}w_{ab}(f_b-f_a)$ for a column observable $f$, and a row probability vector evolves by $p'=pQ$.

For any observable $f:E\to\mathbb R$, write $\pi(f):=\sum_{a\in E}\pi_af_a$. For $f,g:E\to\mathbb R$, define $\langle f,g\rangle_\pi:=\sum_{a\in E}\pi_af_ag_a$. Since $E$ is finite and every $\pi_a>0$, all real functions on $E$ belong to this finite-dimensional real inner-product space, denoted $L^2(E,\pi)$; equality in it is pointwise equality.

The associated jump-chain construction waits an exponential time of rate $q_a$ in state $a$ and then selects state $b\ne a$ with probability $w_{ab}/q_a$, using fresh independent random choices at successive jumps. Here an exponential time of rate $q>0$ has survival probability $\Pr(\tau>t)=e^{-qt}$ for $t\ge0$. The Ionescu–Tulcea construction [[thm-ionescu-tulcea-construction-of-a-markov-chain]] supplies the countable random sequence under the stated Choice assumption. The theorem on this page proves nonexplosion, identifies the transition semigroup, and establishes the positive reversible spectral gap. This is a finite mathematical rate model, not a derivation of rates from Hamiltonian mechanics.

external_suppliers.interface:
Let $S$ be a finite nonempty set, $H:S\to\mathbb R$, and $\beta>0$. Define $Z=\sum_{s\in S}e^{-\beta H(s)}$ and $\gamma(s)=Z^{-1}e^{-\beta H(s)}$. For every probability vector $p$ on $S$, with $0\log0=0$, its Shannon entropy $H_{\rm Sh}(p)=-\sum_s p(s)\log p(s)$ and relative entropy $D(p\Vert\gamma)=\sum_{p(s)>0}p(s)\log(p(s)/\gamma(s))$ satisfy
$$D(p\Vert\gamma)=-H_{\rm Sh}(p)+\beta\sum_s p(s)H(s)+\log Z\geq0.$$
Equality holds exactly when $p=\gamma$. Equivalently, $\gamma$ is the unique minimizer of $\sum_s p(s)H(s)-\beta^{-1}H_{\rm Sh}(p)$, and the minimum is $-\beta^{-1}\log Z$.

external_suppliers.interface:
Assume Countable Choice for the product-measure extension framework of [[def-countable-choice]] and [[lem-csm-lattice-product-and-measure-compactness]]. Work in the finite-alphabet configuration space $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with its cylinder-generated Borel sigma-algebra. Let the finite-range interaction and its conditional energy be as in [[def-csm-finite-range-lattice-interaction]], and fix $\beta>0$. For a finite $\Lambda\subset\mathbb Z^d$ and exterior configuration $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$, put
$$Z_\Lambda^\eta=\sum_{\tau\in A^\Lambda}e^{-\beta E_\Lambda(\tau\mid\eta)},\qquad \gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)=\frac{\sum_{\tau\in A^\Lambda}f(\tau\eta)e^{-\beta E_\Lambda(\tau\mid\eta)}}{Z_\Lambda^\eta}$$
for bounded measurable $f:X\to\mathbb R$. Here $\gamma_\Lambda f$ denotes the function $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)$, composition is operator composition, and $\mu\gamma_\Lambda(f)=\int\gamma_\Lambda(f\mid\eta)\,d\mu(\eta)$. A proper kernel leaves every exterior-measurable event fixed. A specification is a family $(\gamma_\Lambda)_{\Lambda\text{ finite}}$ of proper probability kernels satisfying $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ whenever $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$. A DLR state is a probability measure $\mu$ on $X$ satisfying $\mu\gamma_\Lambda=\mu$ for every finite $\Lambda$.

For the existence and uniqueness results below, a specification has **finite range** when for every finite $\Delta$ and every cylinder event $C$ the function $\eta\mapsto\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_C\mid\eta)$ depends on only finitely many coordinates of $\eta$. The displayed finite-range Gibbs formula has this property because only finitely many interaction terms meet $\Delta$, and a cylinder indicator depends on only finitely many additional coordinates.

The formula is the candidate Gibbs specification; [[lem-csm-lattice-specification-consistency]] establishes its positive finite normalization, measurability, properness and consistency under the stated hypotheses. The Countable Choice assumption is used for the product-measure construction, not for any finite conditional sum.

external_suppliers.interface: For probability vectors $p,q$ on a finite set $A$, there is a coupling $(X,Y)$ with $\Pr(X\ne Y)=\tfrac12\sum_{a\in A}|p(a)-q(a)|$. For a finite region $\Lambda$ with strictly positive single-site Gibbs conditionals, the random-scan heat-bath chain has the finite-volume Gibbs law as its unique stationary distribution. This chain is an auxiliary finite-state proof device, not a physical time evolution.

external_suppliers.interface:
Assume Countable Choice, $d\geq1$, a finite nonempty alphabet $A$, and a proper, consistent finite-range specification $\gamma$ on $X=A^{\mathbb Z^d}$ with its cylinder-generated Borel $\sigma$-algebra, using [[def-csm-lattice-gibbs-specification]]. Here consistency means $\gamma_\Lambda\gamma_\Delta=\gamma_\Lambda$ for finite $\Delta\subseteq\Lambda$, properness means $\gamma_\Lambda(r_\Lambda^{-1}(D)\mid\eta)=\mathbf1_D(\eta)$ for each exterior-measurable event $D\subseteq A^{\Lambda^c}$ and $\eta\in A^{\Lambda^c}$, where $r_\Lambda:X\to A^{\Lambda^c}$ is coordinate restriction; in compositions and integrals against measures on $X$, every kernel takes the appropriate exterior restriction of the global configuration as its argument, and finite range means each $\gamma_\Delta(\mathbf1_C\mid\cdot)$ for finite $\Delta$ and cylinder event $C$ depends on only finitely many exterior coordinates. Also assume a uniform finite integer radius $R\geq0$ such that each one-site kernel $\gamma_{\{i\}}$ depends only on exterior spins $j$ with $\|i-j\|_\infty\leq R$. For each pair of sites define $c_{ij}$ as the supremum of the half-total-variation change in the one-site conditional law at $i$ when only exterior spin $j$ is changed, where half-total variation for probability vectors $p,q$ on $A$ is $\frac12\sum_{a\in A}|p(a)-q(a)|$, and set $c_{ii}=0$. If
$$c=\sup_i\sum_jc_{ij}<1,$$
then the DLR state is unique. Moreover, for a finite region $\Lambda$ and two exterior conditions $\xi,\zeta$, couple the random-scan finite-volume heat-bath chains by choosing the same uniformly random site and using a maximal coupling of its two single-site conditional laws. A stationary joint law of this pair chain exists. If the distance $\operatorname{dist}_\infty(i,\Lambda^c):=\inf_{j\notin\Lambda}\|i-j\|_\infty$ is at least $r(R+1)$ for a nonnegative integer $r$, then its disagreement probability at $i$ is at most $c^r/(1-c)$. Consequently every local conditional expectation becomes uniformly insensitive to boundary conditions as $\Lambda\uparrow\mathbb Z^d$.

external_suppliers.interface:
Let $S$ be finite nonempty, let $H_0,M:S\to\mathbb R$, fix $\beta>0$, and set $H_t=H_0-tM$ and $Z(t)=\sum_{s\in S}e^{-\beta H_t(s)}$ for $t\in\mathbb R$. For the normalized finite Gibbs law $\gamma_t(s)=Z(t)^{-1}e^{-\beta H_t(s)}$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\log Z(t)=\beta\,\gamma_t(M),\qquad \frac{d^2}{dt^2}\log Z(t)=\beta^2\operatorname{Var}_{\gamma_t}(M)\geq0,$$ where $\operatorname{Var}_{\gamma}(M):=\gamma(M^2)-\gamma(M)^2$.
For fixed $H:S\to\mathbb R$, the corresponding inverse-temperature identities are
$$\frac{d}{d\beta}\log Z(\beta)=-\gamma_\beta(H),\qquad \frac{d^2}{d\beta^2}\log Z(\beta)=\operatorname{Var}_{\gamma_\beta}(H)\geq0.$$
These are finite-state identities; they do not justify differentiating an infinite-volume limit.

external_suppliers.interface:
Fix $d\geq1$. A pair potential is an even Borel function $\phi:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}$. For a finite list of positions $X=(x_1,\ldots,x_N)$, set $U_0=U_1=0$ and
$$U_N(X)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(x_i-x_j).$$
The value $+\infty$ is allowed and represents a forbidden configuration; $-\infty$ is not allowed.

The potential is **stable** if some finite $B\geq0$ satisfies $U_N(X)\geq-BN$ for every $N$ and every $X$. Fix a cell side $\ell>0$ and the half-open cubic tiling $C_k=\ell(k+[0,1)^d)$, $k\in\mathbb Z^d$, and let $n_k(X)$ count the positions of $X$ in $C_k$. The potential is **cell-superstable** if there are constants $A_*>0$ and $B_*\geq0$ such that
$$U_N(X)\geq A_*\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^d}n_k(X)^2-B_*N$$
for every finite configuration; the sum is finite for finite $X$.

For disjoint finite cell-index sets $I,J$, let $W_{I,J}(X)$ be the sum of pair terms with one point in a cell indexed by $I$ and the other in a cell indexed by $J$. The potential is **lower regular** for this tiling if a nonnegative envelope $\Psi:\mathbb Z^d\setminus\{0\}\to[0,\infty)$ exists with $\sum_{k\ne0}\Psi(k)<\infty$ and
$$W_{I,J}(X)\geq-\sum_{k\in I}\sum_{l\in J}\Psi(k-l)n_k(X)n_l(X)$$
for all such $I,J,X$. The ordered-pair convention in this formula is fixed as written.

A **decreasing-integrable tail bound** means that for some $R_0\geq0$ there is a nonnegative nonincreasing function $\psi:[R_0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ such that $|\phi(x)|\leq\psi(|x|)$ for $|x|\geq R_0$ and $\int_{R_0}^{\infty}\psi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr<\infty$. This explicit envelope condition is stronger than bare Lebesgue integrability of an arbitrary signed tail. Stability, cell-superstability, lower regularity, and a tail bound are separate properties; none is inferred from finite range alone.

external_suppliers.interface:
Let $\mathcal A$ be finite, let $p$ be a probability vector on $\mathcal A$, and set $S:=\operatorname{supp}(p)=\{a\in\mathcal A:p(a)>0\}$. Then $S$ is finite nonempty and $p(a)>0$ on $S$. For each $n\ge1$, use the finite product law $p^{\otimes n}$ from [[def-it-finite-alphabet-product-law]] and [[lem-it-finite-product-law-is-iid]] on $\mathcal A^n$, and let $X_1^{(n)},\ldots,X_n^{(n)}$ be its coordinate maps. Let $\widehat P_n$ be the empirical type of this coordinate word, viewed as a $\Delta(\mathcal A)$-valued map. Identify the support simplex
$$\Delta(S):=\{q\in[0,1]^S:\sum_{a\in S}q(a)=1\}$$
with the face of $\Delta(\mathcal A)$ whose coordinates outside $S$ vanish. Then $\widehat P_n\in\Delta(S)$ almost surely under $p^{\otimes n}$. For any set $\Gamma\subseteq\Delta(S)$, let $\Gamma^\circ$ and $\overline\Gamma$ denote its interior and closure in the relative topology induced by $\|\cdot\|_1$.
With $\inf\varnothing=+\infty$ and $\ln0=-\infty$,
$$\liminf_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\ln p^{\otimes n}(\widehat P_n\in\Gamma)\ge-\inf_{q\in\Gamma^\circ}D(q\|p),$$
and
$$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\ln p^{\otimes n}(\widehat P_n\in\Gamma)\le-\inf_{q\in\overline\Gamma}D(q\|p).$$
For every $n\ge1$ the finite upper bound
$$p^{\otimes n}(\widehat P_n\in\Gamma)\le(n+1)^{|S|-1}\exp\!\left(-n\inf_{q\in\overline\Gamma}D(q\|p)\right)$$
also holds. If the two infima agree, the limit exists and equals their negative common value. Equivalently, when $S\ne\mathcal A$, one may restrict the product sample space to $S^n$ without changing these event probabilities, since every word outside $S^n$ has zero product mass.

external_suppliers.interface:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as defined in [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $n\ge1$, let $K\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be symmetric positive definite, and let $\beta>0$. For $x\in\mathbb R^n$ put $H(x)=\tfrac12x^{\mathsf T}Kx$, and use the Euclidean Lebesgue measure $\lambda_n$ to define the density $Z^{-1}e^{-\beta H(x)}$. Then

$$Z=\int_{\mathbb R^n}e^{-\beta H(x)}dx=\left(\frac{2\pi}{\beta}\right)^{n/2}(\det K)^{-1/2},\quad \mathbb E[x]=0,\quad \mathbb E[xx^{\mathsf T}]=\beta^{-1}K^{-1},\quad \mathbb E[H]=\frac{n}{2\beta}.$$

Positive definiteness and $\beta>0$ are essential for this normalized full-space Gaussian. The unrestricted identity $\mathbb E[x\,H'(x)]=\beta^{-1}$ is false without a boundary hypothesis: on $[-L,L]$ with $L>0$ and $H\equiv0$, the normalized expectation on the left is $0$.

external_suppliers.interface:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

external_suppliers.interface: For every commutative ring $R$, loop value $\delta\in R$, and objects $m,n,p,q\ge0$, the raw diagram data of [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]] form a strict monoidal category $\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)$ with hom-modules $M_R(m,n)$ and the stated $R$-bilinear stacking composition. Consequently $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal{TL}_R(\delta)}(n)=\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is a unital associative $R$-algebra whose underlying $R$-module is free on its noncrossing pairing diagrams.

external_suppliers.interface:
Fix an integer $d\ge1$, a side length $L>0$ in metres, a mass $m>0$ in kilograms, and a smooth even periodic pair potential $W\in C^\infty(\mathbb T_L^d;\mathbb R)$ in joules, where $\mathbb T_L^d:=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^d$ is the flat position torus and even means $W(-q)=W(q)$. For each finite integer $N\ge1$, the phase space is $(T^*\mathbb T_L^d)^N$ with canonical coordinates $z_i=(q_i,p_i)$, $q_i\in\mathbb T_L^d$ in metres and $p_i\in\mathbb R^d$ in kilogram-metres per second. In position charts obtained by lifting torus coordinates to $\mathbb R^d$, define

$$\theta_N:=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{a=1}^d p_i^a\,dq_i^a,\qquad \omega_N:=-d\theta_N=\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{a=1}^d dq_i^a\wedge dp_i^a.$$

Overlaps of these position charts are translations by vectors in $L\mathbb Z^d$, with the same momentum coordinates, so $dq_i^a$ and $p_i^a$ agree on overlaps. Thus the displayed forms glue globally on $(T^*\mathbb T_L^d)^N$; $\omega_N$ is closed and nondegenerate by its displayed coordinate matrix. Both forms have action units of joule-seconds. Use the Hamiltonian convention $\iota_{X_{H_N}}\omega_N=dH_N$ of [[def-csm-dk-hamiltonian-flow-measure]]. The finite-particle Hamiltonian, with energy in joules, is

$$H_N(q_1,\ldots,q_N,p_1,\ldots,p_N)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\frac{|p_i|^2}{2m}+\frac1N\sum_{1\le i<j\le N}W(q_i-q_j).$$

The interaction force is $K(q):=-\nabla_qW(q)$, in newtons. It is bounded and globally Lipschitz on the compact torus; evenness of $W$ makes $K$ odd and $K(0)=0$. Hamilton's equations in the canonical convention are

$$\dot q_i=\frac{p_i}{m},\qquad \dot p_i=\frac1N\sum_{j\ne i}K(q_i-q_j).$$

For any chosen momentum scale $P_0>0$ in kilogram-metres per second, define the time scale $\tau_0:=mL/P_0$ in seconds, dimensionless variables $x_i:=q_i/L\in\mathbb T^d:=(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^d$, $v_i:=p_i/P_0$, and $s:=t/\tau_0$. Define the dimensionless potential $\Phi(x):=mW(Lx)/P_0^2$ and force $k(x):=-\nabla_x\Phi(x)$. Then the equations become

$$x_i'=v_i,\qquad v_i'=\frac1N\sum_{j\ne i}k(x_i-x_j),$$

where prime denotes derivative with respect to dimensionless time $s$. Here
$\|Dk\|_\infty:=\sup_{x\in\mathbb T^d}\|Dk(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}$, with operator
norm induced by the Euclidean norm, and $\|k\|_\infty:=\sup_x|k(x)|$; the
constants $A:=\|Dk\|_\infty$ and $B:=\|k\|_\infty$ are finite and
dimensionless. This is the selected smooth periodic mean-field scaling; it is
not the hard-sphere Boltzmann-Grad scaling.

external_suppliers.interface:
Assume AC. The **Metropolis–Hastings procedure** takes as input a standard-Borel
space $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ ([[def-standard-borel-space]]), a target
probability measure $\pi$ ([[def-probability-measure]]), and a probability
kernel $Q$ from $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X)$ to itself
([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]).

1. On the product sigma-algebra ([[def-product-sigma-algebra-and-finite-product-sigma-algebras]]),
form the proposal-flow measure $\mu$ ([[def-measure]]) on
$\mathsf X\times\mathsf X$ by
$$\mu(C)=\int_{\mathsf X}Q(x,C_x)\,\pi(dx),\qquad C_x=\{y:(x,y)\in C\}.$$
This is a probability measure by [[lem-prior-and-model-kernel-define-joint-law]].
Let $\tau(x,y)=(y,x)$ and set $\mu^{\mathsf T}(C)=\mu(\tau^{-1}C)$.

2. Set $\eta=\mu\wedge\mu^{\mathsf T}$, the greatest measure dominated by both
flows. Put $\lambda_0=\mu+\mu^{\mathsf T}$, which is a finite measure by
[[thm-nonnegative-weighted-sums-of-measures]], and choose nonnegative measurable
representatives $f=d\mu/d\lambda_0$ and $g=d\mu^{\mathsf T}/d\lambda_0$
with $f+g=1$ everywhere after modification on a $\lambda_0$-null set. Define
$$\alpha(x,y)=\begin{cases}\min\{1,g(x,y)/f(x,y)\},&f(x,y)>0,\\1,&f(x,y)=0.\end{cases}$$
This is a jointly measurable version of $d\eta/d\mu$ taking values in $[0,1]$.

3. For $x\in\mathsf X$, compute the integrated acceptance probability
$$a(x)=\int_{\mathsf X}\alpha(x,y)\,Q(x,dy)$$
and rejection probability $r(x)=1-a(x)$.

4. Return the transition rule
$$P(x,A)=\int_{\mathsf X}\mathbf1_A(y)\alpha(x,y)\,Q(x,dy)+\mathbf1_A(x)r(x),\qquad A\in\mathcal X.$$
The second term retains every rejected proposal as a self-transition.

The item [[lem-common-submeasure-and-bounded-radon-nikodym-density]] proves the
common-submeasure construction and density-version claims in step 2.

Assume AC and the hypotheses of [[alg-metropolis-hastings-kernel]]. Its output
$P$ is a probability kernel, the joint measure
$J_P(dx,dy)=\pi(dx)P(x,dy)$ is symmetric under $(x,y)\mapsto(y,x)$, and $\pi$
is invariant for $P$. Symmetry of this joint measure is reversibility. No
irreducibility, uniqueness, convergence-rate, or central limit theorem
conclusion is asserted.

Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,m)$ be a sigma-finite measure space, let $w\ge0$ be
measurable with $m(\{w>0\})>0$, let $r\ge1$ and let
$X=(X_1,\ldots,X_r):\Omega\to\mathbb R^r$ be measurable and finite, and let
$\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be open. For
each compact $K\subset\Theta$, assume an integrable $G_K$ satisfies
$$w(x)e^{\theta\cdot X(x)}\left(1+\sum_a|X_a(x)|^2\right)\le G_K(x)\quad(\theta\in K).$$
Then $Z(\theta)=\int w e^{\theta\cdot X}\,dm$ is finite, strictly positive
and $C^2$, and the probability density $\rho_\theta=Z(\theta)^{-1}we^{\theta\cdot X}$
defines $dP_\theta=\rho_\theta\,dm$ as in [[def-measure-with-density]].
For any integrable real $A$, write $\langle A\rangle_\theta:=\int A\,dP_\theta$;
for square-integrable real $A,B$, define
$\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(A,B):=\int(A-\langle A\rangle_\theta)(B-\langle B\rangle_\theta)\,dP_\theta$.
These extend the phase-space conventions of
[[def-csm-statistical-state-observable]] to the present measure space.
Then
$$\partial_a\log Z=\langle X_a\rangle_\theta,\qquad \partial_a\partial_b\log Z=\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X_a,X_b).$$
In particular, the Hessian of $\log Z$ is positive semidefinite.

external_suppliers.interface:
Let
$$\mathsf E=((\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y),\Theta,(P_\theta)_{\theta\in\Theta})$$
be a statistical experiment ([[def-statistical-experiment]]). Equip the parameter set with a specified measurable structure $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ ([[def-measurable-space]]). A **proper Bayesian model** based on this experiment consists of a prior probability measure $\Pi$ on $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ ([[def-probability-measure]]) and a probability kernel $K$ from $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ to $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$ ([[def-measure-kernel-and-probability-kernel]]) that represents the experiment:
$$K(\theta,B)=P_\theta(B)\qquad(\theta\in\Theta,\ B\in\mathcal Y).$$
Thus $\theta\mapsto K(\theta,B)$ is $\mathcal T$-measurable for every data event $B$, as required for a parameter-measurable model ([[def-parameter-measurable-statistical-model-as-markov-kernel]]). The family of measures in a parametric model alone does not supply this parameter sigma-algebra or measurability condition ([[def-parametric-statistical-model]]).

The word **proper** means that the prior is a probability measure. A sigma-finite improper prior is not a proper Bayesian model in this definition; fixed-data posterior normalizers for such priors are handled separately.

external_suppliers.interface:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). In a proper Bayesian model, suppose both parameter and data spaces $(\Theta,\mathcal T)$ and $(\mathsf Y,\mathcal Y)$ are standard Borel ([[def-standard-borel-space]]). Let $J$ be the joint prior-predictive law and let $J_Y$ be its data marginal. There is a data-indexed posterior probability kernel $y\mapsto\Pi_y$ such that, for all $A\in\mathcal T$ and $B\in\mathcal Y$,
$$J(A\times B)=\int_B\Pi_y(A)\,J_Y(dy),\qquad J_Y(B)=\int_\Theta K(\theta,B)\,\Pi(d\theta).$$
The composition $\Pi_{Y(\omega)}$ is a posterior RCD. Any two data-indexed posterior kernels agree as probability measures outside one measurable $J_Y$-null set. On any measurable $J_Y$-null set, the conditional-law identities do not select a pointwise value: replacing the kernel there by the prior $\Pi$ preserves the identities.

external_suppliers.interface:
Let $(\mathsf X,\mathcal X,\mu)$ be a measure space. An **unnormalized target density** is a measurable function $\tilde p:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ with
$$Z_p:=\int_{\mathsf X}\tilde p\,d\mu\in(0,\infty).$$
The target probability measure is $\pi(dx)=\tilde p(x)\mu(dx)/Z_p$. A **proposal density** is a measurable $q:\mathsf X\to[0,\infty)$ with $\int q\,d\mu=1$; write $Q(dx)=q(x)\mu(dx)$. The input integrand $f:\mathsf X\to\mathbb R$ is measurable, and the input sample $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ is IID with law $Q$, in the sense of [[def-identically-distributed-and-iid-random-variables]]. The normalizing constant $Z_p$ is known for this algorithm.

**Admissible conditions for an unbiased estimate:** $n\ge1$, $q>0$ $\mu$-almost everywhere on $\{x:f(x)\tilde p(x)\ne0\}$, and the random variable
$$Y:=\begin{cases}f(X_1)\tilde p(X_1)/(Z_pq(X_1)),&q(X_1)>0,\\0,&q(X_1)=0\end{cases}$$
is integrable under $Q$. The support condition makes the value on $q=0$ immaterial to the target integral.

**Well-defined weights:** The reciprocal map $r(s)=1/s$ for $s>0$ and $r(s)=0$ for $s\le0$ is Borel. Its composition with $q$, multiplied by the measurable inputs, makes the piecewise weight and weighted integrand measurable ([[thm-composition-with-borel-functions-preserves-measurability]], [[thm-arithmetic-and-lattice-operations-preserve-measurability]]).

**Procedure and output:** For each supplied draw $X_i$, set $Y_i=f(X_i)\tilde p(X_i)/(Z_pq(X_i))$ when $q(X_i)>0$ and set $Y_i=0$ otherwise. Return
$$\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}:=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^nY_i.$$
Separate variance and central limit claims require the corresponding weighted second-moment hypothesis.

external_suppliers.interface:
Use the hypotheses and notation of [[thm-ordinary-importance-sampling-is-unbiased]]. Define
$$Y_i:=\begin{cases}f(X_i)\tilde p(X_i)/(Z_pq(X_i)),&q(X_i)>0,\\0,&q(X_i)=0\end{cases},\qquad \theta:=\int f\,d\pi,\qquad \sigma^2:=\operatorname{Var}_Q(Y_1).$$
If $\mathbb E_Q[Y_1^2]<\infty$, then $\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}$ has finite variance and
$$\operatorname{Var}_Q(\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}})=\frac{\sigma^2}{n}=\frac1n\left(\frac1{Z_p^2}\int_{\{q>0\}}\frac{f(x)^2\tilde p(x)^2}{q(x)}\,d\mu(x)-\theta^2\right).$$
This finite-sample conclusion is choice-free. For the central limit conclusion, let $(X_i)_{i\ge1}$ be an IID sequence with law $Q$, and apply the estimator to its first $n$ draws for each $n\ge1$. If, in addition, AC holds, then
$$\sqrt n\bigl(\hat\mu_{\mathrm{IS}}-\theta\bigr)\Rightarrow N(0,\sigma^2).$$
No finite variance or normal-limit claim is made when the weighted second moment is infinite.

external_suppliers.interface: For finite real intervals on which the operation is defined, each finite result of addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and squaring in [[def-outward-rounded-interval-and-ball-operations]] contains the exact set of values of the corresponding real operation. For a finite expression directed acyclic graph using these operations, supply each input node with a finite interval containing all its admissible values and each constant node with a finite interval containing its exact value. If all operation nodes return finite interval results, the interval computed at every node contains its exact value for every admissible input assignment; in particular, the root interval contains the exact range. A non-finite status makes no finite enclosure claim.

planned_suppliers.interface: For a finite nonempty alphabet S, equip S^(Z^d) with the product topology and cylinder sigma algebra; local convergence is convergence of every finite-coordinate marginal.

For a finite matrix L with nonnegative off-diagonal entries and zero row sums, bounded real f and every initial law, M_t=f(X_t)-f(X_0)-integral_0^t Lf(X_s)ds is square integrable with bracket integral_0^t (L(f²)-2fLf)(X_s)ds.
Every square-integrable cadlag martingale M with M_0=0 obeys E sup_(t<=T)|M_t|²<=4 E|M_T|².
For finite joint laws P,Q with Q positive, D(P||Q)=D(P_X||Q_X)+sum_x P_X(x)D(P_(Y|x)||Q_(Y|x)); grouping events decreases relative entropy.
For a finite-spin specification, c_ij is the maximal total variation change of the i conditional law after changing only spin j; C has zero diagonal.
If C has nonnegative entries and row sums <=c<1, two Gibbs measures with conditional discrepancies bounded by b satisfy |mu f-nu f|<=sum_i delta_i(f)[(I-C)^(-1)b]_i for every bounded cylinder f.

For translation-invariant finite-range Ising kernels with the uniform Dobrushin row bound c<1 on an open parameter interval, bounded-spin correlations are absolutely summable and the limiting magnetization derivative is the covariance sum.
An abstract polymer model is a countable set with reflexive symmetric incompatibility, activities z, and finite-volume partition function given by compatible subsets.
Under sum_(eta incompatible gamma)|z_eta|exp(a_eta)<=a_gamma, the absolute rooted connected-cluster sum with root gamma is bounded by exp(a_gamma).
A strict locally uniform polymer majorant implies a zero-free finite partition function and normally convergent connected expansion for log Z in that activity domain.

For a measurable stable translation-invariant pair potential v on R^d with stability constant B, beta>0 and finite C_beta=integral_R^d |exp(-beta v)-1|, pin x_1=0. For n>=2 the integral over x_2,...,x_n of the absolute connected-graph Mayer sum is at most exp(2 beta B n)n^(n-2) C_beta^(n-1).
The stable regular continuum pressure Mayer series converges absolutely when |z|exp(2 beta B+1) C_beta<1, with termwise activity derivatives on compact subdomains.
If X_n has an LDP with rate I on compact K and F is continuous, the log-Laplace limit is sup_K(F-I), and normalized exp(nF) tilting gives rate I-F+sup_K(F-I).

For finite alphabet p>0 and continuous h, canonical macrostates minimize D(q||p)+beta h(q); a constrained macrostate at energy u is canonical at beta precisely when it minimizes the constrained entropy cost and u maximizes s(v)-beta v.

For J>0 and H=0 the Curie–Weiss canonical magnetization minimizer is uniquely zero when beta J<=1 and consists of +/-m_beta when beta J>1, where m_beta is the unique positive solution m=tanh(beta Jm).
For finite periodic lattice and m²,kappa>0 define K=m²I+kappa(-Delta) and the Gaussian probability with precision K.
The infinite-lattice Fourier integral for massless covariance at fixed separation is finite in d>2 and its diagonal diverges in d<=2.

Input a finite positive definite precision matrix and an ordered finite list of retained-coordinate subsets. At each step permute retained coordinates first, partition into A,B,C, solve C X=B^T and output A-BX plus the exact log-determinant normalization increment; terminate after the list.
The block-RG procedure terminates after its finite list and returns the exact retained Gaussian marginals and normalization factors.
For smooth compactly supported fields under x=b xprime and phi(x)=b^(-(d-2)/2) phi_prime(xprime), the gradient action is invariant and the quartic coefficient transforms by b^(4-d).
For finite graph, integer Q>=2 and nonnegative v_e, define spin weights and random-cluster weights Q^k(A) product_e v_e with their finite positive normalizers.
The component-coloring joint law has the Potts and FK marginals and satisfies P(sigma_x=sigma_y)=1/Q+(1-1/Q)P(x connected y).

Input a finite ordered strip graph, Q>=2 and v_e>=0; start from empty connectivity, process each edge by identity plus v_e times join, detach vertices after their final edge multiplying by Q on closed components, then sum terminal weights.
The connectivity transfer terminates after finitely many edges and returns Z_FK exactly in exact arithmetic.

For a finite connected planar graph with specified free exterior boundary, the FK partition polynomial can be rewritten as a medial noncrossing-loop sum with loop value sqrt(Q), with the graph-dependent Euler prefactor and edge weights explicitly retained.
Define SSEP on (Z/NZ)^d by nearest-neighbor unordered-bond swaps at rate N², with empirical measure N^(-d)sum eta_x delta_(x/N).
For smooth periodic G, the empirical-field martingale drift is <pi,Delta_N G> and its bracket on [0,T] is bounded by C_G T N^(-d).

If initial empirical measures converge in probability to rho_0 dx with 0<=rho_0<=1, then for every smooth periodic G and T finite, sup_(t<=T)|<pi_t^N,G>-integral rho_t G| tends to zero in probability, where rho_t is the heat solution with datum rho_0.
For smooth periodic rho in [epsilon,1-epsilon] and j satisfying continuity, define I(rho,j;0,T)=one quarter integral |j+grad rho|²/[rho(1-rho)].
For the smooth admissible paths, I(rho,j)-I(theta rho,-theta j)=integral f(rho_T)-integral f(rho_0), where theta reverses time and f(r)=r log r+(1-r)log(1-r).
For smooth strictly interior target rho on a torus with mean rbar in (0,1), the infinite-horizon action infimum from homogeneous rbar is integral [rho log(rho/rbar)+(1-rho)log((1-rho)/(1-rbar))].
On the periodic line define two-velocity transport with speeds +/-c/epsilon, turning rate lambda/epsilon², c,lambda>0, and nonnegative smooth initial densities.
The two-velocity evolution preserves nonnegativity and mass and contracts the L² norm of the pair.
For smooth well-prepared periodic initial data f_plus=f_minus=rho_0/2, rho^epsilon converges in L² uniformly on bounded time intervals to heat evolution with D=c²/(2lambda).
For finite irreducible q with symmetric support and invariant pi>0, define S_T as the sum over jumps of log[pi_x q_xy/(pi_y q_yx)] for a stationary path.
The stationary path and its time reversal have likelihood ratio exp(S_T); E exp(-S_T)=1 and P(S_T in ds)=exp(s)P(S_T in -ds).

For finite energies E_x(t) of class C^1 on [0,T], beta>0, finite bounded continuous jump rates with instantaneous Gibbs detailed balance and initial law pi_0, define W=integral_0^T partial_t E_(X_t)(t)dt and Z_t=sum_x exp(-beta E_x(t)). Then E exp(-beta W)=Z_T/Z_0.

Input finite positive Gibbs weights, initial configuration and integer t>=0. Repeat t times: choose a site uniformly, draw independent U uniform on [0,1], and replace that spin by the first cumulative conditional interval containing U. Output final configuration.
For n sites and Dobrushin row and column sums bounded by c<1, the random-scan heat-bath chain has worst-start TV distance <=n exp(-(1-c)t/n).

Input ferromagnetic finite Ising model and a stored iid site/uniform stream indexed by negative integers; replay common updates from all-minus and all-plus from horizons -1,-2,-4,...; stop when outputs agree and return that common state.
With finite positive Ising heat-bath conditionals and finite sites, monotone CFTP terminates almost surely and its output has exactly the Gibbs law.
For integer Q>=2 ferromagnetic finite Potts weights, activate each equal-spin edge independently with probability v_e/(1+v_e), then recolor each bond component independently uniformly in Q colors.
The Swendsen–Wang procedure preserves the finite Potts Gibbs law; it terminates after finite bond and component operations.
For finite X, positive reference weights and statistic T:X->R^k, define A(theta)=log sum_x w(x)exp(theta.T(x)) and the normalized Gibbs family.
The Hessian of A is Cov_theta(T), and it is positive definite for every theta iff no nonzero linear combination of T is constant on X.
In a minimal finite exponential family the iid MLE is finite and unique precisely when the sample sufficient-statistic mean lies in the relative interior of conv(T(X)).

A latent Gibbs observation model consists of a proper prior on theta, finite Gibbs state pi_theta and a probability kernel K(y|sigma,theta); its likelihood is sum_sigma pi_theta(sigma)K(y|sigma,theta).
For the latent Gibbs model on standard-Borel parameter/data spaces with proper prior, a posterior kernel exists under AC and is unique only prior-predictive almost everywhere.
For real q>=1, p in (0,1), finite graph and boundary partition xi, define FK mass proportional to p^o(1-p)^c q^(k after wiring xi).
Finite FK with q>=1 is positively associated, satisfies the spatial Markov property, and is stochastically increasing in p and boundary wiring.
On a finite planar graph with dual boundary convention, complementing edges sends FK(p,q) to dual FK(pstar,q), where pstar/(1-pstar)=q(1-p)/p.

For q>=1 and fixed alpha>1, at p_sd=sqrt(q)/(1+sqrt(q)) there is c(alpha,q)>0 such that every admissible rectangle of side alpha n by n in a periodic square torus of side m>alpha n has horizontal crossing probability at least c(alpha,q).

For fixed q>=1 and epsilon>0, a finite FK model with p in [epsilon,1-epsilon] and any increasing event A has an edge e with I_A(e)=P(A|omega_e=1)-P(A|omega_e=0) at least c(q,epsilon)P(A)(1-P(A))log(|E|)/|E| for |E|>=2.
For q>=1, periodic crossing estimates at p_sd, the FK differential influence inequality and boundary monotonicity imply percolation for p>p_sd and exponential two-point decay for p<p_sd on Z².
For every real q>=1 the square-lattice FK threshold is p_c=sqrt(q)/(1+sqrt(q)); below p_c every infinite-volume FK state has two-point connectivity bounded by C(p,q)exp(-c(p,q)|x-y|).
For integer Q>=2 and square-lattice Potts energy -J sum_edge delta_spin with J>0, the critical inverse temperature obeys beta_c J=log(1+sqrt(Q)).
For positive weights on a finite space and iid pi_0 samples, the sample mean of w_1/w_0 is unbiased for Z_1/Z_0 and its relative variance is chi²(pi_1||pi_0)/n.
Input positive finite weights w_0,...,w_K and independent stages of n_k>=1 iid exact pi_k draws; compute each mean w_(k+1)/w_k and return their product.
The independent bridge-ratio output is unbiased for Z_K/Z_0 and its relative second moment equals product_k[1+chi²(pi_(k+1)||pi_k)/n_k].

Input a finite enumerated configuration space, finite rational intervals enclosing every strictly positive weight, and finite observable intervals. Add and multiply by outward-rounded interval operations, then divide observable-weight sum by partition interval only if its lower bound is positive; otherwise return unresolved denominator.
The interval finite-partition procedure terminates and encloses the exact Z and, on successful division, the exact normalized expectation for every admissible input weight and observable choice.
